meaning.evidence: Every fact survives: the 227-year-old hemlock planted in 1791, "gusts reportedly up to 70 mph (about 110 km/h)", the whisky barrel, "no relation to the 42nd President Bill Clinton", Jackson's magnolia and the Pioneer Cabin sequoia.

sense.evidence: The few changes fit: "knocked over on Friday by gusts", "Other historic US trees to come down lately", "km/h" for the Australian unit.

authenticity.evidence: What it says is natural Australian news English ("the people running the Mount Vernon estate", "no relation to"), but almost nothing in it is distinctively Australian.

register.evidence: Far lighter than level 3: it is a plain-English rewrite with hardly a local word, such as "Mount Vernon was Washington's own estate, where he worked through most of his two terms".

tone.evidence: Keeps the straight news tone: "According to Mount Vernon officials, the hemlock is the best documented tree on the estate."

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly, the original's awkward first sentence untangled: "on Mount Vernon, the Virginia estate of the first US President George Washington".

variety.evidence: Too little slang to vary; nothing is repeated either.
